summary:
Reviewed the entire round-1 packet and the 62a0cf0..1cf5a7e implementation at HEAD 1cf5a7ed6c3f909ef65d6eb8657c9a5f0a0520c3. No previous-round blocking list was supplied, so previous_status is empty. Acceptance is for the K93 candidate under the packet's disclosed-staging rule, not a declaration that all broader ISA 0.9 migration deliverables are complete.

Required K93 hand reproductions: (1) mcx (s,b) t resolves to [s,b0,b1,t], while mcx (b,s) t resolves to [b0,b1,s,t]. With s=1,b=3,t=0 each yields t=1 with +1 phase; b=1 or 2 yields t=0. With s=1,b=3,t=1 each yields t=0. k=3 in both cases; their written identities differ. (2) Under disjoint active r, the same gate has k=3,c=4: r=s=1,b=3 toggles t, and r=0 does not. The published predicate vector covers all 32 inputs. (3) SWAP then MCX maps (p,q,c) to (q XOR [c=3],p,c); the adjoint does MCX before SWAP. Applied to (|0,0,0,0>+|0,0,3,1>)/sqrt(2), in (p,q,c,R) order, it gives (|0,0,0,0>+|1,0,3,1>)/sqrt(2), retaining both positive amplitudes. All agreed with published expectations and execution. Independently evaluating every source gate confirmed all 140 published basis rows; the generator and test expected values are not copied from interpreter execution.

Rubric method 1: derived inc8(255) at tight B=2/3 as (payload,code,steps)=(0,1,2)/(0,0,3). For zero_cause, B=0 gives code 1; B=1,x=0 gives code 1; x=1 at any B>=1 gives effective cause 4; x=0 at B>=2 succeeds with payload 0. All eight x/B cases for B=0..3 passed. Reconstructed the inc8 envelope from isa=0.9, ptr_width=32, JCS signature and six LF-terminated function lines; independent SHA-256 is ed9865300b85a519c2379de98e36e635e72b5b78d8bdfca03dccf9a09aa3df5e. Also independently reproduced K93 fixture envelopes, the witness object hash and full ref-library envelope hash.

Method 2: traced complete step commit/inverse and both printed call/ret inverse lists. For a recursive call at old sp=16,fp=0,depth=1 with R_f=16, C5 sets fp=16,sp=32,depth=2; C5 inverse restores depth=1,sp=16,fp=0 before C3 clears the record and C2 restores callee locations, allowing C1 to clear captured recursive arguments. Return inversion restores the callee fp before delivery and location restoration. The complete-snapshot regression passed. Traced and ran the nested clock call/ret/uncall witness; whole reversal reported exact entry equality and no second effect undo. Independent step-check probes for zero_cause and an MCX-containing lift.perm_call oracle passed every B=0..3 prefix, including idle and fault cases.

Method 3: audited all 33 SPEC-QUESTIONS entries. Read the 0.8-era proposals as historical where the supplied 0.9 clauses supersede them, including free/pinned entries, layout paths, metadata and fixed bindings. No additional K93 reading is necessary; the documentation-status refresh is S1. Method 4: ran every requested grep pattern across Rust source/tests (348 source matches, 3747 test matches). Classified matches as test assertions/fixtures, guarded internal invariants, exact-to-display amplitude conversion or explicit version/device errors; no todo!/unimplemented! stub or newly reachable panic was found in the changed paths. Method 5: compared lifted rows and arithmetic families with object.rs/oracle.rs/machine.rs, the 14 gates with schema.rs/validation.rs/action.rs/quantum.rs, codes 0..10 with fault dispatch/reporting, history and step-frame kinds with their inverses, metadata with the versioned schema tables, and README CLI commands with main.rs. Remaining broad target/launch/realisation-checker work is disclosed staging, not a new K93 omission.

Baseline already supported variable-arity resolved MCX in quantum.rs and whole-wire flattening in the catalog. Scalar admission/execution/borrow resolution were the substantive gaps; the source adapter now supplies explicit ordered bit operands. No persistent resolution cache is reused: the per-compilation borrow cache remaps all formal bits for each actual, and source constructor state is per compilation. The correct 16-row certificate rechecks as Proof and the same-source-hash stale first-bit table rejects. Additional probes covered 129-bit controls, local-copy controls, legal predicate overlap/repetition, and all 16 outcomes of a two-row lifted-MCX oracle.
